actions.authority: senior administrators (citing the board's June 2026 screen-time vote)
actions.summary: All students blocked from generative AI on district devices for 2026-27 while a new Generative AI Ad Hoc Committee reviews instructional use and safeguards; recommendations due by end of the school year. Teachers may still use AI on district devices.
actions.notes: Confirmed by the district by email 2026-09-02, reported 2026-09-03. Previously students 13+ who completed digital-citizenship training could use approved AI tools. Applies to district-owned devices only; no policy yet on personal devices. Not a board vote - administrators acted 'in the spirit of' the board's unanimous June 2026 screen-time limits, so its durability is weaker than a board-adopted policy. Enrollment figure is approximate.

actions.summary: Launched 'Ed', a $6M AI chatbot for families and students, in March 2024; shut it down in June 2024 after the vendor AllHere collapsed, with about $3M paid. The most-covered district AI procurement failure to date.
actions.notes: Kept as history (lifecycle rescinded, so it never counts toward the state's leaning). Inspector-general review of data handling followed; the board nonetheless approved an AI budgeting-portal resolution on 2024-06-18. Enrollment figure is approximate.

actions.authority: board ad hoc committee; vote scheduled 2027-03-09
actions.summary: Deferred rather than decided: in June 2026 the board kept its existing off-and-away phone policy and formed an ad hoc committee instead of acting on AI. The technology policy now gets a February 2027 review and a 2027-03-09 vote, leaving AI decisions to individual schools and teachers in the meantime.
actions.notes: Included as a deliberate non-decision by a top-five California district while LAUSD and NYC moved the other way - the direction 0 is the point. No AI policy is in force at SFUSD as of 2026-09-14. Enrollment approximate.
